title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Two bones, one forearm. Which one is glowing?
This is the right arm, shoulder to wrist.
Which bone is it?
Two bones run along the forearm.
The glowing one is on the thumb side.
It's B. The radius.
Why it matters: a fall on your hand often breaks it near the wrist.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Hit this bone's elbow end and it's not funny. Name it.
Watch the long bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
It runs from your shoulder to your elbow.
The femur is its match, but in your thigh.
It's C. The humerus.
Why it matters: the funny bone tingle is a nerve, not this bone.

title: The Arm
question: What's its everyday name?
lines: This flat, triangle-shaped bone sits on your upper back.
We're looking at the right shoulder from behind.
What's the everyday name of this bone?
The collarbone is a slim bone at the front of the shoulder.
This broad, flat bone glides over your ribs when you move your arm.
It's A. The shoulder blade, or scapula.
Why it matters: it gives your shoulder muscles a wide anchor.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone forms the elbow's point?
lines: Lean on your elbow. This glowing bone is what you feel.
Watch the long forearm bone that's glowing.
Which bone forms the point of the elbow?
The humerus meets the elbow, but it ends above the point.
The point is the olecranon, part of the pinky-side forearm bone.
It's D. The ulna.
Why it matters: your triceps pulls on that point to straighten the arm.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Run a finger along the top of your chest. You can feel this bone.
Look at the glowing bone across the top of the chest.
Which bone is glowing?
The scapula is the broad bone behind the shoulder.
It's C. The clavicle.
Why it matters: it's one of the bones people break most in a fall.

title: The Arm
question: How many bones are in the forearm?
lines: Turn your palm up, then down. How many bones just moved?
Watch the glowing bones of the forearm.
How many bones are in the forearm?
The upper arm has just one: the humerus.
It's C. Two: the radius and the ulna.
Why it matters: two bones let you rotate your palm up and down.

title: The Arm
question: Which girdle do these bones form?
lines: Shrug your shoulders right now. These two bones just moved.
Look at the two glowing bones at the top of the shoulder.
Which girdle do these bones form?
The pelvic girdle does the same job for your legs.
It's B. Together they form the shoulder girdle.
Why it matters: this girdle lets your arm swing in almost any direction.

title: The Arm
question: What's its everyday name?
lines: You can feel this bone just below your neck. What's it called?
Watch the glowing bone across the front of the shoulder.
What's its everyday name?
The shoulder blade is on the back, not the front.
This slim, curved bone runs from the breastbone to the shoulder.
It's A. The collarbone, or clavicle.
Why it matters: it links your arm to the rest of the skeleton.

title: The Arm
question: Which forearm bone is on the thumb side?
lines: Hold your palm up. Which forearm bone sits on your thumb side?
Watch the glowing bone of the forearm.
Which bone is on the thumb side?
The ulna runs along the pinky side instead.
The glowing bone lines up with the thumb.
It's D. The radius.
Why it matters: it turns around the ulna when you rotate your forearm.

title: The Arm
question: How many bones are in the upper arm?
lines: Your upper arm looks simple. Do you know how many bones it holds?
Watch the glowing bone between the shoulder and the elbow.
How many bones are in the upper arm?
The forearm has two bones, but the upper arm has fewer.
One long bone, the humerus, runs from shoulder to elbow.
It's C. Just one, the humerus.
Why it matters: it's the single bone every upper-arm muscle works on.

title: The Arm
question: Which is the longest bone in the arm?
lines: Your arm has five bones. One is much longer than the rest.
Watch the glowing bone in the upper arm.
Which is the longest bone in the arm?
The ulna is long, but it's shorter than this one.
This bone runs from the shoulder socket down to the elbow.
It's B. The humerus.
Why it matters: it's the lever for lifting and throwing.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone holds the shoulder socket?
lines: Your shoulder is a ball and socket. Where is the socket?
Watch the glowing flat bone behind the shoulder.
Which bone holds the socket?
The collarbone connects at the shoulder, but it holds no socket.
The ball is the top of the arm bone. The socket is part of this bone.
It's B. The scapula.
Why it matters: the socket is shallow, so the shoulder moves widely.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone links the arm to the chest?
lines: Muscles hold most of your arm to your body. One bone does too.
Watch the long thin bone glowing near the top of the chest.
Which bone links the arm bones to the chest?
The scapula floats on the back, held mostly by muscles.
Only this bone joins the arm's skeleton to the breastbone.
It's D. The clavicle.
Why it matters: that joint is the arm's only bony link to the trunk.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone is on the pinky side?
lines: Hold out your hand, palm up. Look at your pinky side.
Watch the glowing forearm bone.
Which forearm bone lies on the pinky side?
The radius is the other forearm bone, on the thumb side.
This one forms the point of the elbow too.
It's D. The ulna.
Why it matters: the radius turns around it when you flip your palm.
